expected_at_membrane_boundary_after_comp: post-oxygenator pCO2 returns approximately to inlet pCO2
post-oxygenator O2 saturation returns approximately to inlet saturation
post-oxygenator pO2 returns approximately to the pO2 implied by inlet saturation
expected_in_coupled_patient: true patient pCO2 increases when sweep falls from baseline to zero
patient-directed ECMO blood flow is materially unchanged by sweep loss alone
expected_after_sweep_restoration: post-oxygenator pCO2 decreases from the no-sweep state
post-oxygenator oxygenation again exceeds representative venous inlet oxygenation
coupled patient pCO2 returns approximately toward its pre-failure state
nonzero_sweep_control_rule: at fixed blood flow and FdO2, increasing nonzero sweep primarily improves CO2 clearance
ordinary nonzero sweep titration does not materially change modeled oxygenation
allowed_exceptions: this contract isolates complete sweep-gas flow loss and does not represent oxygenator thrombosis or blood-path obstruction
the current unified patient native venous saturation model can be near fully saturated, so the coupled-patient oxygenation consequence is not used as an acceptance assertion in v1
displayed patient gases may lag true state according to the dynamic display model
FdO2 failure with ongoing gas flow is a distinct fault and requires its own contract
gas-source disconnection and gas-line obstruction may share the zero-effective-sweep endpoint but can have different bedside observations

the model does not represent residual oxygen stored in the oxygenator/gas path; zero-sweep assertions represent a sustained post-transient effective-zero-sweep state rather than an instantaneous response
notes: Zero sweep is treated as zero effective gas-side flow across the membrane lung: no O2 addition and no CO2 removal.
The representative inlet gases are regression inputs for isolating membrane behavior, not patient treatment targets.
This contract asserts directional bedside coherence rather than exact gas-transfer performance for a specific oxygenator.
Evidence review clarifies that the zero-sweep boundary is a post-transient steady-state abstraction; transient residual-gas washout is outside v1.
